helpful: The petition.txt appendix carried the Ninth Circuit opinion text, which let me read the panel's actual contempt reasoning (text-violation alternative ground, McComb reliance) rather than only the parties' framings — decisive for splitting vacate vs affirm mass.
The merits-docket statpack section's per-Term table with the excluded count made the baseline pooling mechanical.
gaps: A merits-stage judgment-class cut (vacated vs reversed vs affirmed conditional on disturbance, by originating circuit) would sharpen the judgment label; the section publishes the aggregate distribution only.
The citation filter on SCOTUS rows is thin (161 of 590k rows carry cites), so known-case lookups for doctrinal anchors like Taggart come back empty; a caption-substring lookup would cover this.
The single citation query cost 1329 ranged GETs / ~348 MB for an empty result — expensive relative to its yield.
notes: Grant-moment merits cell: no merits briefs exist yet, so the cert-stage documents plus the docket skeleton were the whole substantive record; they were sufficient.
